items.html: aqua medicāta — mineral water; classical: Seneca, N.Q. 3.25.9, and Pliny, N.H. 2.222 (medicātās aquās); M-O s.v. mineral water. aqua minerālis — the modern term (Traupman 72).

english: At table: finish your fish / bite it / slow down / oily hands / rinse your mouth / dessert / pastry / chocolate / cream
latin: bellāria, bellāriōrum n. · crustulum, crustulī n.
keywords: dinner table meal finish eat up last bite too big slowly hurry pudding sweets eclair cake biscuit chocolate cream lemon juice

items.html: bellāria, bellāriōrum n. — dessert, sweets (Traupman 71); Varro’s quip via Gellius: bellāria … ea maximē sunt mellīta, quae mellīta nōn sunt — the sweetest desserts are the ones without honey (Gell. 13.11.6).

crustulum, crustulī n. — small pastry, biscuit; serviceable for an éclair and the like. Horace’s teachers coax boys with them: ut puerīs ōlim dant crustula blandī doctōrēs, elementa velint ut discere prīma (Serm. 1.1.25–26).

socolāta, socolātae f. — chocolate (Traupman 70; M-O). crēmum, crēmī n. — cream (Traupman 71, post-classical); flōs lactis — cream (Traupman 71; M-O, from pharmacopoeia Latin). Not cremor, which in L&S is a thick broth.
Comēde tōtum piscem! — Finish all your fish! (perēdō is poetic.)
Sī omnem piscem et omnia holera comēderis, tū quoque accipiēs. — If you eat all your fish and vegetables, you’ll get some too.
Paene cōnfēcistī! Paulum tantum superest. — You’re almost done! There’s only a little left.
Ūnum morsum etiam, deinde bellāria. — One more bite, then dessert. (morsus, morsūs m.: L&S leaves the o unmarked; nothing supports a long vowel.)
Mordē! Nimis magnum est. — Bite it! It’s too big. (mordeō is second conjugation, so mordē.)
Nōlī tantum cibī simul in ōs inserere! Lentius mandūcā! — Don’t put so much food in your mouth at once! Chew more slowly!

Lentē! Festīnāre tē nōlō. — Slowly! I don’t want you to rush (festīnāre tē nōlō, Cic. Fam. 16.11.1). Augustus’ “make haste slowly” was Greek, σπεῦδε βραδέως (Suet. Aug. 25; Gell. 10.11.5); festīnā lentē is the later Latin form.
Vīsne sūcum citreī in pisce? — Do you want lemon juice on your fish? (citreum: see the lemon entry.)
Manūs tuae oleō oblitae sunt! — Your hands are covered in oil! (oblitus, short i, from oblinō; not oblītus from oblīvīscor.)
Prīmum aquam bibe, ut ōs colluās. — Drink some water first, to rinse your mouth (colluō, Pliny).
Utrum māvīs, socolātam an crēmum? — Which do you prefer, chocolate or cream?
Bonum est, nōnne? — It’s good, isn’t it? Hoc nōn vīs? — Don’t you want this?

laganum, laganī n. — pancake (M-O s.v. pancake: laganum Americānum or crassum for the thick kind); classically a flour-and-oil cake (Hor. S. 1.6.115).
laganum Gallicum — crêpe (M-O s.v. pancake: crepe).

items.html: būbula, būbulae f. — beef (Traupman 70; M-O carō būbula); būbulus “of cattle” is classical (Plaut.). porcīna, porcīnae f. — pork (Traupman 72; Plaut.); M-O also suilla, suillae f. (Cels., Plin.).
agnīna, agnīnae f. — lamb (Traupman 71; M-O carō agnīna); vitulīna, vitulīnae f. — veal (Traupman 73; Plaut.); carō ovilla — mutton (M-O; ovillus, Cato).
gallīnācea, gallīnāceae f. — chicken as food (Traupman 70); M-O pullus gallīnāceus (Vives). anatīna, anatīnae f. — duck as food (Traupman 71), substantive of anatīnus (Plaut.).
perna, pernae f. — ham (Traupman 71; M-O; Cato, Agr. 162); perna fūmōsa — smoked ham (Traupman 325): holus fūmōsae cum pede pernae (Hor. S. 2.2.117).
offa porcīna — pork chop (Traupman 72); classically offa is a morsel, ofella a chop (Juv., Mart.). frustum būbulae — steak (Traupman 73, who prints frūstum; the series spelling is frustum).
assum, assī n. — a roast (Traupman 72; assum vitulīnum, roast veal, Cic. Fam. 9.20.1); būbula assa — roast beef (Traupman 68, 72); M-O assum būbulum.
sēmicoctus, -a, -um — rare, half-done (Traupman 68; Col., Plin.); percoctus, -a, -um — well done (Traupman 68; percoquō); M-O parum percoctus — undercooked.
minūtal, minūtālis n. — a dish of minced meat, hash (M-O s.v. hash; Juv. 14.129; Mart.).
Quid est hoc? — Būbula. — What’s this? — Beef. (cf. Corderius, Coll. II 10: Carō est, sed quaenam? — Būbula.)
Dā mihi, quaesō, lībram pernae. — A pound of ham, please.
Utrum sēmicoctam an percoctam māvīs? — Do you want it rare or well done?

items.html: pastillum fartum — sandwich (Traupman 73); pastillum pernā fartum — ham sandwich (325). M-O prefers pānis fartus (or replētus), noting that pastillum, a little loaf, is found only in two grammarians (Varro ap. Charis.; Paul. ex Fest.).
acētāria, acētāriōrum n. — salad (Traupman 72; M-O; Plin. 19.58); commīxta acētāria — mixed salad (Traupman 72).
embamma, embammatis n. — dressing, a sauce to dip in (Traupman 71; M-O s.v. sauce; Col.; Plin.).
liquāmen Magōnicum — mayonnaise (Traupman 72, after Mahón); M-O liquāmen majonēnse, following the vernacular (the o is unmarked there).
ketsupum, ketsupī n. — ketchup (Traupman 71); M-O lycopersicātum, lycopersicātī n., formed like Apicius’ piperātum. Both are modern.

cucumis muriāticus or cucumis muriā conditus — pickled cucumber, pickle (M-O s.v. cucumber: pickle); muria is brine (Cato). Traupman 72 gives salgamum, but L&S has salgamum only as “food, sustenance” (Cod. Just.), so it is not used here.
pōma terrestria frīcta — chips, French fries (Traupman 71); M-O māla terrestria frīcta, batātae frīctae. lāminae pōmōrum terrestrium — crisps (Traupman 363); M-O orbiculī batātae.
Vīsne pastillum pernā fartum? — Do you want a ham sandwich?
Acētāria sine embammate mālō. — I prefer the salad without dressing.

english: Cooking methods: boiled / stew / grill / gridiron / bake / smoked / breaded / whip / mince / dice
latin: ēlixus, ēlixa, ēlixum · crāticula, crāticulae f.
keywords: boiled boil stew stewed simmer slow cook grill gridiron barbecue broil bake baked smoked breaded coated in flour whip beat whisk mince chop finely dice cube

items.html: ēlixus, ēlixa, ēlixum — boiled (Traupman 70; Hor. S. 2.2.74). Plautus contrasts it with assus, roast: ēlixus esse quam assus soleō suāvior (Most. 5.1.66, as cited by L&S). ēlixāre, boil, is late (Apicius; M-O s.v. stew).
lentō igne coquere — stew, cook slowly (Traupman 385); jūrulentum, jūrulentī n. — stew (Traupman 73), from the post-Augustan adjective jūrulentus, “in its juice” (L&S). M-O gives Vives’ jussulenta.

crāticula, crāticulae f. — grill, gridiron (Traupman 71, 276): rāra tibi curvā crāticula sūdet ofellā — “let the gridiron sizzle with a few chops” (Mart. 14.221.1). super crāticulam assāre — grill, barbecue (Traupman 71, 276).
in furnō coquere — bake (Traupman 276; M-O s.v. boil: bake); coquō alone also means bake.
fūmōsus, -a, -um — smoked (Traupman 71, perna fūmōsa; Cato).

farīnā circumlitus — breaded, coated in flour (M-O s.v. breaded, after Mattioli). Traupman 70 gives saligneus, but L&S has salignus, saligneus only as “of willow”; probably a slip for silīgineus, of fine wheat. Not used here.
peragitāre — beat, whip (eggs, cream): rudiculā ligneā peragitāre (Col. 12.46.3; M-O s.v. beat, whip).
minūtim concīdere — chop finely, mince (M-O); tessellātim concīdere — dice (Apic. 4.3; late, L&S).
Ōvum ēlixum mihi placet, nōn frīctum. — I like a boiled egg, not a fried one.
Caepam minūtim concīde. — Chop the onion finely.

english: Sweets and baked treats: sweets / cheesecake / birthday cake / bun / doughnut / croissant / pretzel / jam / popcorn / chewing gum / sugar cube
latin: dulcia, dulcium n. · lībum, lībī n.

items.html: dulcia, dulcium n. — sweets (M-O s.v. sweets; L&S under dulcis); cuppēdia, cuppēdiōrum n. — dainties, treats (L&S; Plaut.). Traupman 70 makes it feminine, cuppēdiae; L&S has the feminine singular only as “daintiness” (Cic. Tusc. 4.26). dulciolum, dulciolī n. — a sweet (Traupman 286; not in L&S). M-O adds tragēmata (Plin.) and cuppēdia saccharīna.
lībum, lībī n. — cake of meal, cheese and honey (Cato, Agr. 75); lībum nātāle — birthday cake (Traupman 70).
savillum, savillī n. — cheesecake (Traupman 70; Cato, Agr. 84: savillum hōc modō facitō); M-O placenta cāseāta (cāseātus, Apul.).

collȳris, collȳridis f. — bun, roll (Traupman 70; L&S: Vulgate, Augustine). lucunculus, lucunculī m. — a kind of pastry (Afranius; Statius; L&S); M-O uses it for doughnut, printed lucunulus. pānis corniculātus — croissant (M-O).

pretiola, pretiolae f. — pretzel (Traupman 72, 364, modern); M-O nōdus pānis; LRL crustulum sale conditum (cited in M-O s.v. pretzel). Traupman’s “muffin”, scriblīta (72), is classically a tart (Cato, Agr. 78; Plaut.); M-O uses it for pizza.

bācārum conditūra — jam (Traupman 335, printed baccārum condītūra; series spelling bāca; L&S has conditūra, from condō, preserve). M-O pōma conditīva (cf. conditīvus, Cato). quilon, quilī n. — jelly (Traupman 71; L&S post-classical, Vegetius).
maizium īnflātum — popcorn (Traupman 363; M-O, after Helfer); LRL maizae grāna tosta (cited in M-O s.v. popcorn).
cummis masticābilis — chewing gum (Traupman 290; cummis, gum, is classical; masticābilis is modern); M-O mastichē, mastichēs f., mastic gum (Plin.; M-O prints masticha).
saccharum cubicum — sugar cube (Traupman 73); M-O sacchari tessella. saccharum pulvereum — icing sugar (Traupman 72); saccharō conditus — candied (M-O).
Ūnum tantum dulciolum, deinde dentēs pūrgābimus. — Just one sweet, then we’ll brush your teeth.
Avia lībum nātāle tibi coquit. — Grandma is baking you a birthday cake.
Hoc lībum ad avum afferāmus. — Let’s take this cake to Grandpa.

fidēlia, fidēliae f. — jar, earthenware pot (M-O; Col.; Pers.): M-O finds it especially apt for a preserving jar; pyxis vitrea — glass jar (M-O).
capsella, capsellae f. — small box (M-O; Petr.); cistula, cistulae f. — little box (Plaut.). fasciculus, fasciculī m. — parcel, package (M-O, after Egger; classically a bundle of letters, Cic.).
cūpa, cūpae f. — barrel, cask (M-O; Caes.); dōlium, dōliī n. — a large storage jar (Traupman 122 gives it for barrel; M-O for vat).
gutus, gutī m. — cruet, narrow-necked oil flask (M-O; Juv.; L&S); acētābulum, acētābulī n. — vinegar vessel, later any small cup (Traupman 402; L&S).
Ubi est extrāculum? Lagoenam aperīre volō. — Where’s the corkscrew? I want to open the bottle.
Mel in fidēliā est; eam operculō claude. — The honey is in the jar; put the lid on it.

blocks.html: gutus: M-O prints gûtus; L&S leaves the u unmarked. Left unmarked. aperculum has no attested quantity; its vowels are short as in aperiō.

items.html: māchina mixtōria — mixer (Traupman 346, mīxtōria); M-O māchina agitātōria, keeping mixtōria for the blender.
māchina coquīnāria — food processor (Traupman 123; Helfer, cited in M-O).
māchina expressōria — juicer (M-O).
māchina caffeāria — coffee maker (Traupman 293; M-O spells it cafeāria); the lexicon follows caffēa.
māchina carnāria — meat grinder (Traupman 344); mola caffeāria — coffee grinder (M-O, spelled cafeāria).
clībanus tostōrius — toaster oven (M-O; clībanus, a small baking oven, Plin.).
discus coctōrius — hob, burner (Traupman 284; M-O); foculus mēnsārius — hotplate (M-O, after Vives); foculus campester — camping stove (M-O, citing LRL, Helfer and Egger).

authepsa, authepsae f. — self-heating cooker, “somewhat like our tea-urns” (L&S): authepsa illa, quam tantō pretiō nūper mercātus est (Cic. Rosc. Am. 133). M-O builds on it: authepsa lenta or coctōrium lentum — slow cooker; coctōrium oryzae — rice cooker; authepsa theāria — samovar.
māchina pānifica — bread maker (M-O).
Ōva et farīnam in māchinā mixtōriā misceāmus. — Let’s mix the eggs and flour in the mixer.
Nōlī discum tangere; ārdet! — Don’t touch the hob; it’s hot!

blocks.html: Why mixtōria, not mīxtōria: Traupman marks the i long, but L&S leaves it unmarked in mixtum, and de Vaan (2008: 382–383) prints mixtum, mixtūra with a short i, explaining mixtum as syncopated from *mixitum. Spanish mestizo and French métis, from Late Latin mixtīcius, also continue a short i. Bennett’s list of hidden quantities has not been checked yet.
